questions.question: Define an ore and explain why a deposit can become an ore when the price of the mineral rises.
questions.expected_answer: An ore is a rock or deposit containing enough of a valuable mineral or metal to be mined and processed at a profit. If the price rises, the income from the same amount of mineral increases, so lower-grade rock that was previously too costly to mine can now be mined profitably, and becomes ore.

questions.question: Compare surface and underground mining, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each and a South African example.
questions.expected_answer: Surface mining removes overburden to reach ore near the surface; it is cheaper and safer but disturbs large areas of land (e.g. Sishen iron ore open pit, opencast coal in Mpumalanga). Underground mining reaches deep ore through shafts and tunnels; it disturbs less surface land but is costlier and more dangerous because of heat, rockbursts, dust and gases (e.g. Mponeng gold mine, nearly 4 km deep).

questions.question: Name three minerals or rocks used in their natural form and state a use for each.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, e.g.: diamonds (jewellery, drill bits); coal (burned for electricity); salt (food, preserving); clay (bricks, pottery); sand and gravel (concrete, roads); granite or marble (building, counters); limestone (cement, treating acidic soil); gypsum (plaster).
